source.title: Bias-variance decomposition of overparameterized regression with random linear features

record.tranche_reason: The study analytically evaluates test error across model and data-to-feature ratios in a random linear-features model, a different method and setting from the original deep-network evidence.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own analytic results and numerical checks for random linear features. The random nonlinear-feature and linear-regression curves in the comparison are reproduced from cited work, so they are not recorded as new results. No values were extracted by estimating plotted coordinates.
record.test_reason: An analytic (cavity-method) and numerical study of ridge-less regression with random linear features. It reports test error, bias and variance across model size (αp) and feature/data ratio (αf). It bears on whether risk peaks at interpolation and falls again in a non-deep model class (V4), and on whether the peak is variance-driven (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find three regimes separated by three phase transitions, two of them to interpolation. Test error and variance, but not bias, diverge there, and beyond interpolation the variance decreases. So the classical trade-off fails in the interpolation regime, though the model lacks the full canonical double-descent shape. Add: overparameterized test error is never worse than underparameterized at fixed αf. Each divergence traces to small Hessian eigenvalues. Linear features add an interpolation transition (αf=1) that nonlinear activations suppress.
record.recipe_differences: The study derives analytic results using a zero-temperature cavity method for random linear features and checks them numerically; it does not reproduce the original deep-network experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The test-error curve depends on the feature/data ratio αf: the αf > 1 and αf < 1 cases behave differently. The paper also distinguishes linear from nonlinear feature models.

fits_no_version.finding: The minimal-bias transition at αf=αp<1 has a vanishing Hessian eigenvalue and a diverging susceptibility, yet test error does not diverge. A transition in model structure need not produce a test-error peak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-error peaks occur only at transitions to interpolation, not at every point where the Hessian spectral gap closes.

fits_no_version.finding: With linear features the interpolation boundary has two branches (αp=1 for αf≥1, and αf=1 for αp≥1). Nonlinear features suppress the αf=1 branch, acting as implicit regularization of small eigenvalues.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The location of the interpolation peak depends on the activation function; nonlinear features suppress the data-matrix-driven divergence.

record.problems: The analytic results are in the thermodynamic limit. Numerical checks use M = M' = 512 for error plots and report only that error bars are small, without giving their magnitudes in the text. The plotted numerical results are averages over simulations; no specific numerical error values are stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No own-result rows omitted. Comparison curves for linear regression and random nonlinear features are described as reproduced from Ref. 35 and were not counted as new results.

untested.parts: All of it; no deep or trained-feature networks are studied, only a convex random-linear-features model.
No explicit sample-size sweep is reported. The 2D phase diagram implicitly varies M, but the authors do not analyse whether more data hurts.
No single effective-complexity measure is proposed to predict peak locations across axes.
Label-noise magnitude is not varied (SNR fixed at 10). Regularization is ridge-less only, so whether tuned ridge removes the peak is untested. Multiple peaks along a single sweep are not reported.

missing.what: Random linear features along the cut αf=αp: test error and variance rise to a divergence at αp=1 then fall, while bias is zero below and rises above threshold. This is an own result of the random-linear-features model.
Test error and variance also diverge along the second interpolation branch αf=1 with αp≥1 (from the 2D phase diagram), with bias finite.
Authors state test error in the overparameterized regime is always at least as small as in the underparameterized regime for fixed αf.
missing.locator: Section III, paragraph after interpolation boundary

record.verdict_notes: V1 removed because the model is a convex random-features model, not a deep trained network; the rows bear on V4 instead. The ridge-less-only analysis means the regularization part of V6 is untested. Figure 3's linear-regression and nonlinear-features panels are reproduced from Ref. 35 (the authors' prior work), correctly excluded. Results are exact only in the thermodynamic limit; numerics use M=512.

versions.untested_parts: Other deep-network architectures and training settings; the study evaluates a random linear-features model with a two-layer linear-network interpretation.
A sample-size sweep near the interpolation threshold testing whether adding data raises test error.
Other model classes beyond the random linear-features model studied here.
Whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample size.
The effect of varying label noise, multiple test-error peaks, and whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
Recounting complexity using an effective number of parameters to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

relationships.condition: Random linear features, αf>1, sweep over αp
relationships.reason: Test error diverges at the interpolation point αp=1 and then decreases monotonically in the overparameterized regime (r1).
relationships.display_finding: Test error diverged at αp=1 and then decreased monotonically in the overparameterized regime.

relationships.condition: Random linear features, αf>1 and αf<1
relationships.reason: Authors say neither case shows the full canonical double-descent shape (r1). For αf<1 the αp sweep is monotone with no peak, because interpolation is not reached (r2).
relationships.display_finding: Neither αf regime showed the full canonical shape; for αf<1, error varied monotonically with αp because interpolation was never reached.

relationships.reason: Variance diverges at the transition to interpolation while squared bias stays finite, so the peak is variance-driven (r4, r5).
relationships.display_finding: Variance diverged at the transition to interpolation while squared bias remained finite.
